title: Sales Qualification Frameworks: BANT, MEDDIC, SPICED & How to Choose
summary: What is MEDDIC? Compare BANT, MEDDIC/MEDDPICC, SPICED, and 5 more sales qualification frameworks — definitions, fit by deal complexity, and how to choose.
body_markdown:
## TL;DR


A sales qualification framework tells your team which deals deserve time. Eight frameworks dominate B2B: **BANT** , **MEDDIC/MEDDPICC** , CHAMP, SPICED, NEAT, ANUM, FAINT, and GPCTBA/C&I. Match the framework to deal complexity and buying-committee size, then coach against the same criteria on every call. Compare the eight side by side before you commit to one. For tooling that scores those frameworks on every call, see the[5 best AI sales coaching tools](https://demodesk.ai/blog/5-best-ai-sales-coaching-tools) .


## MEDDIC definition (quick answer)


**MEDDIC** is a sales qualification framework for complex B2B deals. It stands for **Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain, Champion** . **MEDDPICC** adds **Paper Process** and **Competition** . Use MEDDIC when five or more stakeholders sit on the buying committee and empty fields after three calls are a deal risk, not a paperwork annoyance. For a lighter early-stage filter, start with[BANT](https://demodesk.ai/blog/bant-sales-approach) . Full comparison of all eight frameworks below.


## What is a sales qualification framework?


A qualification framework is a shared checklist for whether a lead is worth pursuing. It answers three questions early: does the prospect have a real need, can they buy, and are they the right fit for what you sell?


Without one, every rep invents their own definition of “qualified.” Pipeline reviews become opinion contests. Forecasts inherit the fiction.


The framework does not replace judgment. It gives the team the same language so empty fields mean something and filled fields mean the same thing to everyone.


## Methodology vs qualification framework


Teams confuse these two constantly.


**Qualification** happens early. It filters: is this lead worth the next call?


**Methodology** runs the whole cycle. It guides how you sell from first conversation to close (Challenger, SPIN, Sandler, and the rest). We cover that separately in[how to choose the right sales methodology](https://demodesk.ai/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-sales-methodology) .


You need both. A methodology without qualification fills the funnel with noise. Qualification without a methodology leaves reps improvising after the first meeting.


## Why teams that qualify consistently win


Shared criteria cut time spent on deals that were never going to close. Conversion improves because reps work accounts that meet budget, need, and authority tests. Forecasts get cleaner because stage names map to evidence, not vibes. Cycles shorten when dead deals exit early instead of lingering until quarter end.


If your CRM already looks complete and still surprises you in pipeline review, the gap is usually qualification consistency, not more fields.


## 8 sales qualification frameworks compared


### 1. BANT


IBM's classic: **Budget, Authority, Need, Timing** .


Best for clear procurement paths and shorter cycles. Weak when buying is collaborative and budget appears late. Use it as a starting conversation structure, not a rigid gate. For AI-assisted BANT and MEDDIC coaching, see[how AI coaching closes the qualification gap](https://demodesk.ai/blog/bant-meddic-ai-coaching-qualification-gap) .


### 2. MEDDIC / MEDDPICC


Built for complex enterprise deals: **Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain, Champion** . MEDDPICC adds **Paper Process** and **Competition** .


Best when five or more stakeholders sit on the buying committee. Overkill for simple SMB deals with one or two decision-makers. Empty fields are the signal: if Economic Buyer is blank after three calls, that is the deal risk. We run MEDDIC on our own pipeline; the write-up is[automated deal scoring with MEDDIC](https://demodesk.ai/blog/automated-deal-scoring-meddic-own-pipeline) . Scorecards:[AI Sales Coaching](https://demodesk.ai/ai-sales-coaching) .


### 3. CHAMP


**Challenges, Authority, Money, Prioritization** (Zorian Rotenberg). Challenges come first, budget later.


Built as a customer-centric alternative to budget-first BANT. Strong for SaaS where ROI conversation matters more than a pre-allocated line item. Also treats Priority as process and plan, not only timeline.


### 4. SPICED


From Winning by Design: **Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical Event, Decision** .


Diagnoses like a doctor: treat the cause, not only the symptom. Works across stages (discovery, handoffs, forecast reviews). Good default when you want outcome language tied to a deadline.


### 5. NEAT


**Needs, Economic Impact, Access to Authority, Timeline** (Harris Consulting Group / Sales Hacker).


BANT alternative for SaaS and complex B2B. Emphasizes deeper needs and ROI, then access to real decision-makers.


### 6. ANUM


Ken Krogue's reorder of BANT: **Authority, Need, Urgency, Money** .


Authority first. Useful when wasted cycles on non-buyers are the main leak. Fits multi-stakeholder B2B with longer cycles.


### 7. FAINT


RAIN Group's variant: **Funds, Authority, Interest, Need, Timing** .


Built for prospects without a pre-defined budget. Funds means capability to spend, not a booked line item. Useful for early-stage markets and newer categories. Can get expensive if Interest is high but Need stays vague.


### 8. GPCTBA/C&I


HubSpot's deep framework: **Goals, Plans, Challenges, Timeline, Budget, Authority** , plus **Consequences** and **Implications** .


Most thorough of the set. Strong when you need goal alignment and a full value story. Heavy for transactional motions; train well or reps drown in questions.


## How to choose


1. **Define the job.** Shorter cycles and clearer budgets lean BANT or ANUM. Complex committees lean MEDDIC. Challenge-first discovery leans CHAMP or SPICED.
2. **Map deal complexity.** Product customization, stakeholder count, and cycle length should drive the pick, not what a popular podcast recommended last month.
3. **Match the team.** A framework your managers will not coach to will not stick. Prefer one you can score on calls.
4. **Hybrid when needed.** Many teams run MEDDIC for enterprise and something lighter for mid-market. That is fine if the rules are written down.
5. **Prefer empty-over-guessed fields.** Whatever you pick, treat blanks as data. Guessed champions destroy trust in the CRM.


Compare the frameworks side by side and adapt the criteria to your ICP.


## How to implement without a theater rollout


- Set one objective (cleaner forecast, higher conversion, shorter cycle) and measure it.
- Train with real call clips, not only slides.
- Pilot on one segment before company-wide.
- Put the criteria in the CRM and in call scorecards so coaching and pipeline review use the same source.
- Review weekly for the first month: which fields stay empty, which reps game the form.
